Diagram of the digestive system of a chicken. A continuous tube starting at the beak, leading to a swollen crop on the neck, then a glandular proventriculus, leading immediately into a large muscular, rounded gizzard. Below the gizzard, a looped small intestine, branching into two blind sacs called caeca, and ending at the cloaca.

Outline of a cow showing the four compartments of its massive stomach filling the left side of the abdominal cavity. The oesophagus leads into the large Rumen (filling most of the space), which connects to the smaller Reticulum near the front. The Reticulum leads to the spherical Omasum, which connects to the elongated Abomasum at the bottom, finally leading into the intestines. Arrows indicate the flow of food, with a two-way arrow in the oesophagus to show regurgitation.
